'''Hinke Maria Osinga''' (born 25 December 1969)<ref>[http://alba.ub.rug.nl/promotorum/?page=showPerson&promovendus_id=5193 Hinke Maria Osinga] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160815224621/http://alba.ub.rug.nl/promotorum/?page=showPerson&promovendus_id=5193 |date=15 August 2016 }} at the Album Promotorum - Bibliotheek der Rijksuniversiteit Groningen</ref> is a Dutch mathematician and an expert in [[dynamical system]]s. She works as a professor of [[applied mathematics]] at the [[University of Auckland]] in New Zealand.<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=https://www.math.auckland.ac.nz/~hinke/cv.html|title=Curriculum vitae: Hinke Osinga|access-date=8 October 2015}}.</ref> As well as for her research, she is known as a creator of [[mathematical art]].

==Education and career==
Osinga earned a master's degree in 1991 and a Ph.D. in 1996 from the [[University of Groningen]].<ref name="cv"/> Her doctoral dissertation, jointly supervised by [[dynamical system]]s theorist [[Henk Broer]] and [[computational geometry|computational geometer]] Gert Vegter, was on the computation of [[invariant manifold]]s.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=50983}}</ref> 

After postdoctoral studies at [[The Geometry Center]] and the [[California Institute of Technology]], and a short-term lecturership at the [[University of Exeter]], she became a lecturer at the [[University of Bristol]] in 2001, and was promoted to reader and professor there in 2005 and 2011, respectively. She moved to Auckland in 2011,<ref name="cv"/> becoming the first female mathematics professor at Auckland and the second in New Zealand.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.math.auckland.ac.nz/en/about/news-and-events/news/news-2011/2011/12/22/Staff-arrivals-and-departures-in-semester-two.html|title=Staff arrivals and departures in semester two|publisher=University of Auckland Department of Mathematics|date=21 December 2011|access-date=8 October 2015|archive-date=24 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190124234208/https://www.math.auckland.ac.nz/en/about/news-and-events/news/news-2011/2011/12/22/Staff-arrivals-and-departures-in-semester-two.html|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

==Mathematical art==
In 2004 Osinga created a [[crochet]]ed visualization of the Lorenz manifold, an invariant manifold for the [[Lorenz system]], and published the crochet pattern for her work with her husband [[Bernd Krauskopf]]; the resulting [[Mathematics and fiber arts|mathematical textile artwork]] involved over 25,000 crochet stitches, and measured nearly a meter across.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.theguardian.com/education/2004/dec/16/research.highereducation3|title=Scientists crochet chaos|first=Donald|last=McLeod|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=16 December 2004}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/03/18/AR2007031801483.html|title=In the loop|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=19 March 2007|first=Paul|last=Richard}}.</ref> Osinga and Krauskopf later collaborated with artist Benjamin Storch on a stainless steel sculpture that provides another interpretation of the same mathematical system.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.siam.org/pdf/news/1718.pdf|title=Lorenz system offers manifold possibilities for art|first=Barry A.|last=Cipra|author-link=Barry Arthur Cipra|journal=SIAM News|volume=43|issue=2|date=March 2010|access-date=9 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304190558/http://www.siam.org/pdf/news/1718.pdf|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Osinga was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2014, speaking on "Mathematics in Science and Technology".<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|access-date=1 October 2015|archive-date=24 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171124141541/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByLastname.php|url-status=dead}}.</ref> In 2015 she was elected as a [[fellow]] of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] "for contributions to theory and computational methods for dynamical systems."<ref>{{citation|url=http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2015|title=SIAM Fellows: Class of 2015|publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]]|access-date=8 October 2015}}.</ref>  In October 2016 she became the first female mathematician elected to the Royal Society of New Zealand.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nzmathsoc.org.nz|title=NZ Mathematical Society bulletin}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/news/diverse-range-of-top-researchers-and-scholars-elected-as-fellows/|title=Royal Society 2016 Fellows}}</ref> She was awarded the [[Aitken Lectureship]] in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LMS-NZMS Forder and Aitken Lectureships {{!}} London Mathematical Society |url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/events/lectures/forder-and-aitken-lectureship |access-date=2023-12-13 |website=www.lms.ac.uk}}</ref>

In 2017 Osinga was selected as one of the Royal Society Te Apārangi's "[[150 women in 150 words]]", celebrating the contributions of women to knowledge in New Zealand.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hinke Osinga|url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/150th-anniversary/150-women-in-150-words/1968-2017/hinke-osinga/|access-date=2021-05-11|website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref> The same year she received the Moyal Medal from Macquarie University.<ref>{{Cite web| url=https://www.mq.edu.au/faculty-of-science-and-engineering/departments-and-schools/school-of-mathematical-and-physical-sciences/engage-with-us/moyal-medal|title=Moyal Medal recipients}}</ref>
